findings.title: Failed browser runs can overstate how many new cases were exercised
findings.evidence: The finally block writes new_cases_exercised=len(new) regardless of how far the browser checks progressed. An assertion failure before the per-question loop still produces the full planned count. The JSON report has no run status or captured Python exception, although the process exits nonzero.
findings.impact: An uploaded partial report can be mistaken for evidence that all new questions were tested. The user explicitly requires reporting tests actually completed; this affects evidence accuracy, not the reader answer/storage code.
findings.recommendation: Track IDs only after each question completes the requested checks. Record planned_cases separately from completed_case_ids/count, and record passed/failed status plus exception details while preserving a nonzero exit on failure.
findings.validation_needed: Exercise a deliberately failing run before the question loop and after one question; ensure neither report claims all cases and both indicate failure. Confirm the normal successful run reports all completed IDs.
findings.resolution: Verifier appends a question ID only after that question completes all its checks, records planned and completed counts separately, and captures failed/passed state plus exception type/message while re-raising the failure.
findings.resolution_verification: Read the final control flow and injected RuntimeError before browser startup through a mock Playwright context. main re-raised it and emitted failed status, planned=46, exercised=0, IDs=[], and the actual exception. No browser or HTTP execution is claimed by this failure-path test.

findings.title: A related archive item carrying a hold warning remained in the default pool
findings.evidence: The MA-CASE-0795 hold included MA-CASE-0349 among affected_archive_ids, but MA-CASE-0349 was initially still recommended. The ledger validation of archive warning IDs against the default pool caught this actual intersection.
findings.impact: A question displaying the review-hold warning could still be included by the unfiltered default practice selection.
findings.resolution: Parent inspected the original item, added MA-CASE-0349 as an explicit default hold, added a builder rejection of archive-warning/default intersection, and the triage reviewer updated its own finding. Original question bytes and answer keys were retained.
findings.resolution_verification: Final selection: 7 held representatives, 21 original IDs with notices, zero intersection with 443 recommended IDs. MA-CASE-0349 is explicitly held and absent from the default. The rebuilt 355-row ledger records 46 rewritten, 1 reuse, 7 hold, 301 not yet implemented.

limitations: No Playwright package or Chromium configuration is available in this peer shell. No local HTTP, production HTTP, mobile screenshot, actual localStorage browser or download/import interaction is claimed as executed by this reviewer.
Reviewed hashes identify the source-freeze snapshot after both findings were resolved. GitHub CI, final commit identity and production browser verification remain separate gates.
This is code and data-flow review. It does not independently certify pharmacy law, every explanation, psychometric difficulty or absence of semantic duplicates.

Existing safeState/import behavior was not redesigned. Manual import replaces the current state; malformed/unknown-ID recovery and stale multi-tab state are pre-existing limitations outside the new revision mapping.

content_version is descriptive metadata; the reader keys history by question_id. Future meaning/key changes to a published MA-RW question must continue using a new ID and retain the prior item, rather than relying on a version-number change alone.
